# the contributor audit: oriented area, cap pyramids, and parity-preserving redistribution



## Oriented planar section body

Read `candidate 915dc3adcfe3fcf0`
in full, including its weighted section. Each supporting allocation has the
stated area measure. An outside allocated facet can be replaced by a shorter
flat body for NORMAL area purposes only; its tangential moments are explicitly
not preserved. The effective cap representatives can all be chosen inside
their own fibers. Their Minkowski integral lies in the Minkowski fiber sum.

In dimension two, additivity of surface-area measure makes that integral a
translate of beta B+J. Support inequalities yield J inside (1-beta)B after
translation. Complementary allocations give a separate translation of -J
inside beta B. Measurable support functions and the distributional planar
support identity justify arbitrary probability cap laws. The triangle
asymmetry calculation gives 4/9 under the stated equal homothetic-cap
hypothesis. It supplies no reduction to that hypothesis.

Nonnegative affine base weights are legitimate under the full affine moment
stress. Their integer mean gives a compatible Minkowski inclusion into one
actual fiber. The section measure is reweighted at the same time; the proof
does not identify it with the original section measure or obtain parity
weighting from affine weights.

## Higher-dimensional obstruction and oriented pyramid bound

Read the following in full:

- `candidate 455c254ad09b8374`;
- `candidate 600f7b09ccd06ced`;
- `candidate aee564c922d3f5fe`.

The simplex surface scaling and asymmetry disprove the proposed reflected
Blaschke containment in every d>=3, even for a minimal full-rank critical
circuit. The fixed-cube reconstruction has exactly the displayed facet
areas. Its section body becomes arbitrarily long as one axis weight tends
to zero. Its ordinary deepest point, exact cap masses and signed boundary
stress are all actual. These examples do not involve a mixed-integer
counterexample or an unaudited body reconstruction.

For the scalar replacement, the pyramid over the actual section with a
farthest captured apex is contained in the cap. Its volume is section area
times height divided by d. This proves the mixed-volume lower bound and its
nonnegative remainder. The mixed-volume order is B once and -J repeated
d-1 times. The simplex retains the factor d from orientation; the cube
shows why the section term alone has no universal Gamma lower bound.

The labeled identity keeps coarea normalization: its homogeneous factor is
(h_Kz(u)-c+a.z)T_Hz, with no extra |u|. Inside allocations weaken the
pyramid and outside allocations have zero height. Strict full fibers keep
their whole captured mass in the remainder; pure-base caps are handled
separately. The threshold-cancellation formula retains all errors before
using actual section means. A common FULL section mean and normal balance
suffice. A group-average base mean alone does not.

Compatibility has the stated unfavorable sign: the own-fiber support
expression equals the mixed support expression plus a NONNEGATIVE deficit.
Therefore the exact cap identity subtracts that deficit. The cube examples
verify that it cannot be silently discarded. Joint bounded record/section
convergence preserves the all-status identity and its actual allocations.

## Arithmetic redistribution and tangential defect addition

Read `candidate 73e20ccf5e0e5f17`
in full. The two affine roof slopes change by the same amount, giving an
actual compatible path with fixed total and parity masses. The supporting
majorant proves the unique optimum over the entire concave parameter class;
the clipping formula checks every cap normal at the proposed middle source.
The endpoint bounds and steep middle caps establish global deepestness.
The exact derivative includes the CHANGING covariance. The coefficient
bound proves strict descent throughout the stated small-buffer range.
This excludes this stratum from joint minimality and refutes parity-mass
interchangeability. It does not cover two nonempty deepest status strata.

Also read Section 8 of
`candidate 9a1deed5372bf5ee`.
The two exponential floors give pointwise rates two and one on the lower
roof, with a uniform bound permitting dominated convergence. The resulting
density has the stated jump and fails log-concavity on the interval. The
one-row source remains interior. As stated in the source, it is neither a
deepest-source nor a physically stationary example.

the contributor reran the companion exact checks: planar 2,529; Blaschke obstructions
587; ordinary pyramid 5,316; labeled pyramid 12,313; arithmetic redistribution
3,740; tangential profiles 3,541. All pass. The general conclusions rely on
the geometric proofs, not on these finite calculations.
